title: A Place of His Own
story:
As twilight settled over the knoll, the colorful paper kites drifted slowly down into the valley, and James walked back down the winding dirt path beside Don Tadeo. The quiet village of Aldea San Gabriel was bathed in the soft lavender glow of dusk, its weathered adobe walls cooling after the sunny afternoon. For sixty-three days, James had traveled from tree to stone, from archive to terrace, always carrying his home on his back. Now, stepping through the wide timber doorway of the old outbuilding behind the carpentry shop, he felt a clear and steady sense of arrival.

Here was a place for his brass compass to rest beside the window. Here was a place for his smooth green sea-glass to catch the morning sun. Here was a place for his clay bird whistle, his polished cog, and his map canister, each set neatly along the smooth cedar shelf Don Tadeo had helped him mount. James swept away the last bits of wood shavings from the corner, piling fresh, fragrant cedar curls into a soft, dry nest near the hearth nook.

Through the open door, he could hear the gentle sounds of the village coming to rest: a distant dog barking twice, the creak of a closing shutter, and the low, comforting hum of Don Tadeo tidying up his workspace next door. James sat back on his heels and looked around the small room. The drafty floorboards had been patched, the old tiles above his head kept out the sky, and the scent of cut pine filled the air.

Don Tadeo paused in the doorway before heading home, leaning on his walking cane. He offered a warm, quiet nod toward the newly arranged space, satisfied to see the forgotten shed filled with life again. When the old carpenter turned and vanished into the blue evening, James curled into his nest of cedar flakes, watching a single bright star appear through the square window above his door.
location: The Old Shed behind Don Tadeo's workshop, Aldea San Gabriel
